model_fitness.best_available_model: Patient-derived iPSC neurons (and isogenic CDKL5 variant knock-in lines) carrying the specific splice/pseudoexon allele, with phospho-EB2 immunoassay as readout; Cdkl5 knockout mouse neurons as the null reference.
model_fitness.captures_relevant_mechanism: Yes for the proximal mechanism: splice correction acts on CDKL5 pre-mRNA in the nucleus, and the direct functional consequence (EB2 phosphorylation) is measurable in patient-derived neurons (EVIDENCE, PMID:30266824; PMID:39033321).
model_fitness.captures_relevant_cell_type: Partially: iPSC-derived cortical excitatory neurons are the relevant lineage, but GABAergic interneuron and visual-cortex circuit biology are not represented, and X-inactivation mosaicism is lost in clonal iPSC lines.
model_fitness.measurable_phenotype: Percent full-length vs aberrant CDKL5 transcript (RT-PCR/long-read), CDKL5 protein level, and phospho-EB2/total EB2 ratio; secondary: microtubule dynamics and dendritic arbor.
model_fitness.important_limitations: No animal model carries a human splice variant and Cdkl5 knockout mice have no spontaneous seizures (EVIDENCE, PMID:24838000), so seizure efficacy cannot be tested preclinically. Human-sequence dependence of the ASO also blocks mouse efficacy testing.

plan.critical_question: Does a denominator exist? I.e. what fraction of reported CDKL5 alleles are output-limited and splice-correctable (cryptic splice site, deep-intronic pseudoexon, leaky splice variant retaining some full-length product), and in at least one such patient's neurons can a steric-block ASO restore full-length CDKL5 transcript and phospho-EB2?
plan.proposed_experiment: Two-stage, cheap-first. Stage 1 (weeks, in silico/database, no bench cost): systematically classify all reported CDKL5 variants in public variant and patient-registry datasets into deletion / frameshift-truncating / nonsense / missense / splice-region / deep-intronic, and within the splice class flag those predicted to create cryptic sites or pseudoexons with retained partial normal splicing. Output a count of candidate splice-correctable individuals worldwide. Proceed only if this exceeds a pre-set threshold. Stage 2 (only if Stage 1 passes): for 1-3 candidate alleles, build the minimal functional system - patient fibroblast/iPSC-derived neurons where available, otherwise a CDKL5 minigene or full-locus construct carrying the variant in a neuronal line - and screen a tiled walk of 2'-MOE/2'-OMe phosphorothioate steric-block ASOs (15-20 mers, ~5 nt step) across the aberrant splice element. Measure full-length CDKL5 mRNA fraction, CDKL5 protein, and phospho-EB2/EB2 by quantitative immunoassay, with AAV- or plasmid-delivered wild-type CDKL5 as the positive control ceiling (the manipulation already shown to raise phospho-EB2 in vivo, PMID:39033321) and scrambled ASO as negative control. Run a parallel gymnotic/free-uptake arm in neurons to confirm activity without transfection reagent, since that is the clinically relevant uptake mode. Explicitly do NOT pursue the poison-exon sub-strategy until a separate, small RNA-seq/long-read experiment on human neuronal CDKL5 transcripts demonstrates that a non-productive splicing element actually exists - that element was not established in retrieved evidence (EVIDENCE, contradictory, source: none retrieved).
plan.model: Stage 1: public variant/registry datasets (no model). Stage 2: patient-derived iPSC cortical neurons carrying a splice allele, plus a CDKL5 minigene reporter in a human neuronal line as the fast-cycling surrogate.
plan.primary_readout: Fraction of full-length CDKL5 mRNA and the phospho-EB2/total-EB2 ratio in ASO-treated versus control patient neurons, expressed as percent of the isogenic wild-type/positive-control ceiling.
plan.supportive_result: Stage 1 identifies a cohort of meaningful size (team should set the bar explicitly, e.g. tens rather than single digits of splice-correctable individuals) AND Stage 2 shows a lead ASO restoring a substantial fraction of full-length transcript with a clearly measurable rise in phospho-EB2 toward the wild-type ceiling, under gymnotic uptake. Decision: advance the n-of-few splice-ASO path for that specific allele class, following the established patient-specific ASO regulatory precedent (EVIDENCE, PMID:34412058), and in parallel commission the reversibility/timing study that governs all restoration modalities.
plan.negative_result: Either Stage 1 shows the splice-correctable set is a handful of individuals worldwide (the predicted dominant failure mode: denominator, not chemistry), or Stage 2 ASOs shift transcript without a detectable phospho-EB2 change. Decision: stop the generalizable CDKL5 splice-ASO programme; retain the tiling protocol as a dormant, reusable n-of-1 capability to be triggered only when an individual patient with a qualifying allele presents and a sponsor exists. Do not spend further on the poison-exon arm absent a demonstrated element.
plan.decision_enabled: Whether to fund a CDKL5 splice-switching ASO programme at all, versus parking it as an on-demand n-of-1 capability. Stage 1 costs almost nothing and can kill the programme before any bench spend - that is the point of the ordering.

model_fitness.best_available_model: For the therapeutic question: none adequate - no neuron-tropic LNP with human data was identified (EVIDENCE, contradictory, source: none retrieved), so no model can test the clinical hypothesis. For the re-scoped research-tool question: Cdkl5-null and patient-derived neurons receiving dose- and time-controlled CDKL5 mRNA in vitro, plus Cdkl5 knockout mice for timing studies.
model_fitness.captures_relevant_mechanism: As a therapeutic test, no: any CSF-LNP experiment would mostly transfect ependyma, meninges and glia rather than deep forebrain neurons, so bulk phospho-EB2 could read positive while the disease-relevant cells are untouched (INFERENCE, contradictory). As a tool, yes: mRNA delivers catalytically competent CDKL5 and phospho-EB2 reports its activity (EVIDENCE, PMID:39033321).
model_fitness.captures_relevant_cell_type: In culture yes (cortical excitatory and GABAergic neurons can both be generated); in vivo the required cell type is precisely the one current LNPs do not reach.
model_fitness.measurable_phenotype: Dose-resolved phospho-EB2/EB2 versus CDKL5 protein level; dendritic arborization; for timing, visual evoked potentials and dendritic morphology in knockout mice after restoration at defined ages.
model_fitness.important_limitations: mRNA gives days of protein against a lifelong developmental requirement; chronic repeat intrathecal LNP dosing in infants has no safety precedent. Knockout mice lack spontaneous seizures (EVIDENCE, PMID:24838000), so the seizure endpoint is unavailable.

plan.critical_question: Do not ask 'can mRNA treat CDD' - the delivery vehicle does not exist at clinical maturity, so that question is not answerable and the therapeutic arm should be closed now. The question worth paying for is the one mRNA is uniquely good at answering and that governs every restoration modality: how much CDKL5 protein, in what fraction of neurons, and for how long, is enough to normalize phospho-EB2 and dendritic phenotypes - and is a transient pulse sufficient or is continuous presence required?
plan.proposed_experiment: Re-scope to a tool experiment, three arms. (A) Dose-response: transfect Cdkl5-null mouse neurons and CDD patient-derived neurons with graded amounts of chemically modified CDKL5 mRNA; plot CDKL5 protein against phospho-EB2/EB2 and dendritic arbor metrics to define the threshold fraction of wild-type CDKL5 needed, and test for any decline at supraphysiological levels (overexpression toxicity). (B) Duration: single mRNA pulse versus repeated pulses, with phospho-EB2 and dendritic morphology sampled as protein decays, to learn whether the phenotype tracks instantaneous kinase activity or integrates it over time. (C) Mosaic-threshold mimic: co-culture or mix transfected and untransfected null neurons at defined ratios (e.g. 10/25/50/75%) and ask whether benefit is cell-autonomous or whether a corrected minority rescues network-level measures (synaptic maturation, multi-electrode-array network activity). Use the same mRNA reagent to express individual patient missense alleles for the variant-function catalogue, classifying each as null, hypomorphic or dominant-negative by whether it raises phospho-EB2 alone and whether it suppresses the activity of co-expressed wild-type CDKL5 - the dominant-negative test that gates the entire missense-stabilization arm.
plan.model: Primary: Cdkl5 knockout mouse primary cortical/hippocampal neurons and CDD patient-derived iPSC cortical neurons in culture, with mixed-genotype co-cultures for the mosaicism arm.
plan.primary_readout: Quantitative phospho-EB2/total-EB2 dose-response curve against CDKL5 protein level, with dendritic arborization and MEA network activity as functional secondaries; for the catalogue, per-allele phospho-EB2 with and without co-expressed wild type.
plan.supportive_result: A clear threshold emerges (e.g. partial restoration in a minority of neurons normalizes phospho-EB2 and dendritic metrics), and benefit persists beyond the protein's presence. Decision: this lowers the bar for every restoration modality, justifies the timing/reversibility study in knockout mice, and - only if a neuron-tropic CNS delivery vehicle later reaches clinical maturity - would re-open the mRNA therapeutic question. The missense catalogue simultaneously tells the small-molecule arm whether stabilization is safe to pursue.
plan.negative_result: Phenotypes require near-complete, continuous CDKL5 in nearly all neurons, or correction is strictly cell-autonomous with no network rescue. Decision: definitively abandon transient-expression modalities for CDD, and down-weight any approach that cannot achieve broad, sustained, pan-neuronal correction. If missense alleles prove dominant-negative, kill the chaperone/stabilization arm outright.
plan.decision_enabled: Closes the mRNA therapeutic arm now (no vehicle), while extracting the one piece of information the modality can cheaply provide - the dose, duration and mosaic-fraction threshold plus the dominant-negative test - which is the shared gating question for the ASO and small-molecule arms. Avoids the named failure mode of building on a non-existent vehicle and of bulk-tissue PD assays reading false positive from non-neuronal cells.

model_fitness.best_available_model: CDD patient-derived neurons carrying defined nonsense alleles (for readthrough) or kinase-domain missense alleles (for stabilization), with phospho-EB2/EB2 as the common readout; plus a cell-free or cellular reporter carrying the patient's exact stop codon in its native sequence context for rapid readthrough-efficiency ranking.
model_fitness.captures_relevant_mechanism: Yes for readthrough: the mechanism is codon-context dependent and the relevant context is the patient's own CDKL5 sequence, which these models contain. For missense stabilization, patient neurons report both protein level and whether the stabilized protein is catalytically productive - the key distinction, since an ATP-site ligand could stabilize while inhibiting.
model_fitness.captures_relevant_cell_type: Partially - iPSC cortical neurons are the right lineage; interneurons and visual-cortex circuits are absent, and clonal lines do not reproduce X-inactivation mosaicism.
model_fitness.measurable_phenotype: Full-length CDKL5 protein by quantitative immunoassay and phospho-EB2/total-EB2; for stabilization also mutant protein half-life (cycloheximide chase) and specific activity per unit protein.
model_fitness.important_limitations: Ataluren was already trialled in CDKL5 nonsense patients and completed without yielding a therapy (EVIDENCE, contradictory, NCT02758626; outcome not retrieved, so this is suggestive, not proof of failure). Neuronal CNS exposure and readthrough efficiency of ataluren were not retrieved and must be treated as unknown. No CDKL5 stabilizer exists and ChEMBL lists no curated mechanism for the target (EVIDENCE, mcp__rp__chembl_target_drugs (CDKL5)), so the chaperone arm has no starting chemistry.

plan.critical_question: Can any available readthrough agent raise full-length CDKL5 protein in neurons carrying patient nonsense alleles by enough to move phospho-EB2 measurably toward wild type - and, separately and prerequisitely, are kinase-domain missense variants hypomorphic (stabilization helps) or dominant-negative (stabilization harms)?
plan.proposed_experiment: Run the cheap disqualifying test first. Arm 1 (readthrough, weeks): treat patient-derived neurons bearing 3-5 distinct CDKL5 nonsense alleles spanning codon contexts with available readthrough and NMD-inhibiting agents, alone and in combination, across a tolerated dose range; quantify full-length CDKL5 protein and phospho-EB2/EB2 against the wild-type ceiling and against an orthogonal CDKL5-restoration positive control (the manipulation shown to raise phospho-EB2, PMID:39033321). Pre-specify the minimum phospho-EB2 shift that would count, informed by the dose-threshold curve from the mRNA tool experiment; if that threshold is not yet known, run the two in parallel because the readthrough result is uninterpretable without it. Arm 2 (variant-function catalogue and dominant-negative test, run before any chemistry spend): express a panel of patient kinase-domain missense alleles in CDKL5-null neurons and measure phospho-EB2 to classify each as null or hypomorphic; then co-express each with wild-type CDKL5 and test whether it suppresses wild-type-driven phospho-EB2 - a drop identifies a dominant-negative allele. Only alleles that are hypomorphic and non-suppressing, and whose protein is destabilized rather than catalytically dead (cycloheximide chase plus activity-per-protein), are legitimate chaperone targets. Only if such alleles exist in non-trivial numbers should a stabilizer discovery effort start, and it should be designed from the outset to screen for stabilization without loss of catalytic output (paired thermal-shift/protein-level and phospho-EB2 assays) rather than for binding alone.
plan.model: CDD patient-derived iPSC cortical neurons with defined nonsense and missense alleles; CDKL5-null neurons as the expression background for the catalogue; native-context stop-codon reporters for rapid readthrough ranking.
plan.primary_readout: Full-length CDKL5 protein and phospho-EB2/total-EB2 as percent of wild type, per allele and per agent; for the catalogue, per-allele phospho-EB2 alone and in the presence of wild-type CDKL5.
plan.supportive_result: A readthrough or NMD-modulating agent raises full-length CDKL5 and produces a phospho-EB2 shift at or above the pre-specified threshold in neurons at achievable exposures - decision: pursue that agent in the nonsense subset with phospho-EB2 as a candidate pharmacodynamic biomarker, and first resolve its neuronal CNS exposure, which is currently unknown. Separately, if a meaningful set of alleles is hypomorphic, destabilized and non-suppressing, decision: initiate a stabilizer discovery programme with the paired stabilization-plus-activity screen.
plan.negative_result: Readthrough produces only a few percent full-length protein with no phospho-EB2 movement (the predicted failure mode) - decision: close the readthrough arm for CDD and do not repeat the clinical attempt. If missense kinase-domain alleles are predominantly catalytically dead or dominant-negative, decision: do not start chaperone chemistry at all, since stabilization would either do nothing or increase a harmful species. Redirect resources toward modalities that supply new functional CDKL5 rather than rehabilitating mutant alleles.
plan.decision_enabled: Decides whether either small-molecule arm deserves funding, using experiments that cost orders of magnitude less than the programmes they gate. The dominant-negative co-expression test in particular can kill the chaperone arm before any screening spend, and it resolves one of the disease's named major unknowns.
